data.title: Insulin Sensitivity & Glucose Disposal
data.mission: Sustain insulin-sensitive glucose disposal so post-meal glucose clears efficiently without prolonged metabolic strain.
data.summary: Insulin helps tissues take up and store circulating glucose after a meal. The effectiveness of that response depends on cellular signalling and the condition of muscle, liver and fat tissue. Exercise training can improve measured insulin action even without weight loss. Magnesium also participates in insulin-receptor function, with deficiency experiments showing impaired action. These routes concern the capacity to handle glucose already available in the circulation.
data.dose_sensitivity: Effects depend on the tested exposure, preparation and study population; no universal dose is established.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Resistant-starch effects on insulin-sensitive glucose disposal are context-dependent
scientific_findings.finding_statement: A small placebo-controlled human supplementation study found higher clamp insulin sensitivity and forearm glucose clearance; a later type-2-diabetes trial did not establish a clamp improvement.
scientific_findings.finding_summary: A small placebo-controlled human supplementation study found higher clamp insulin sensitivity and forearm glucose clearance; a later type-2-diabetes trial did not establish a clamp improvement.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Defined oral resistant-starch supplementation modulated clamp-measured insulin sensitivity and post-meal forearm glucose clearance in a small human study.
scientific_findings.synthesis: A small placebo-controlled human supplementation study found higher clamp insulin sensitivity and forearm glucose clearance; a later type-2-diabetes trial did not establish a clamp improvement.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Preparation-, dose- and population-specific. The positive study used 30 g/day for four weeks in ten healthy participants; this is not an effective whole-food dose. Preserve the later 40 g/day type-2-diabetes null. SCFA mediation and universal benefit are unestablished; no brain or ADHD inference. Numerical SEC remains pending full-method appraisal; no factor is forced.

system_optimisation_practices.input: Six-hour early eating window with weight-maintenance feeding

evidence_source.finding_role: Mechanistic home only; intervention efficacy and SEC come from the separately cited primary trial, not this Finding.

system_optimisation_practices.evidence_limitation: OGTT-derived index, not clamp disposal, tissue signalling or a directly measured circadian mechanism. Fasting and OGTT glucose unchanged; hs-CRP, IL-6 and cortisol unchanged. Eight male completers, unmasked supervised efficacy trial; four withdrawals. Eating-window duration and early timing coupled; pretest fast unmatched. Sequence/period effects affected some other outcomes, not the selected index. Fasting triglycerides and total cholesterol increased; not a uniformly beneficial metabolic profile. Highly supervised protocol does not establish general feasibility or an unsupervised fasting prescription.

moa.description: Early timing and prolonged fasting may alter metabolic handling; neither circadian mediation nor intracellular insulin signalling was isolated.
moa.evidenceQualification: Observed endpoint does not identify causal mediation; no collapsed mechanism summary proposed.

biologicalRelationship.pmRelevance: Insulin-response index is relevant to PM3, with surrogate limitations; no automatic transfer to hormonal/circadian PMs or glucose-disposal flux.

system_optimisation_practices.study_context: 12 enrolled, eight completers; randomised concealed allocation, approximately seven-week washout. Matched calories/composition, supervised meals, dinner by 15:00. Completer mixed models include sequence and period; fasting duration before testing differed.
system_optimisation_practices.sec_assessed_proposition: In eight men with prediabetes completing the crossover, five weeks of early six-hour feeding reduced the OGTT-derived incremental insulin/glucose AUC ratio compared with a twelve-hour eating schedule.
